newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Credireal's base price 121.3 mln reais.
newsitem.headline: Credireal's base price 121.3 mln reais.

text.p: A controlling stake in Minas Gerais state bank Credireal will be sold for a minimum price of 121.3 million reais at a privatization auction Thursday, state officials said Monday.
The base price was set after a 10 percent voting stake reserved to staff was fully acquired by bank employees, retirees and pension fund.
The staff was allowed to buy the shares at a 50 percent discount. The bank's total minimum price had been set at 130.8 million reais.
Minas Gerais state government will sell 687.03 million voting shares and 299.6 million preferred shares at Thursday's auction on the Minas Gerais-Espirito Santo-Brasilia Stock Exchange (BOVMESB).
Eight financial institutions have pre-qualified for the Credireal sale.

They are Credit Commerciale de France's Banco CCF Brasil; Bank of Boston Corp's Brazil unit; General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corp; Banco Industrial e Comercial (Bicbanco); Banco Noroeste ; Companhia de Investimentos Latinoamericana; Tabal Participacoes, and Varejo S.A. Administracao e Participacao.
Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper reported today that CCF and General Electric Capital had dropped out of the running.
No officials at the banks were immediately available for comment on the report.

Credireal, formally known as Banco de Credito Real de Minas Gerais SA, is the second Brazilian state-owned bank due to be privatized. The first was Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, which was bought by Brazil's second largest private bank Banco Itau in June.
Credireal bank has 86 branches, of which 42 are in Minas Gerais state.
